label: Ubiquiti airCube ACB-ISP home Wi-Fi AP
description: Ubiquiti airCube ISP (ACB-ISP) - 4x 10/100 Fast Ethernet ports with a controllable 24 V passive PoE passthrough on the WAN port for an airMAX CPE, 802.11n 2x2 on 2.4 GHz (300 Mbps), powered by 24 V passive PoE on LAN port 1 or a 5 V micro-USB adapter. 5 W maximum draw.
notes: Everything here is 100M: four Fast Ethernet ports and a 2.4 GHz 802.11n radio, so this is a WISP subscriber box, not the gigabit dual-band AP its name suggests. The PoE is *passive* and passes through to the CPE on the WAN port (24 V on pairs 4,5 / 7,8) - the page publishes no wattage for it, so no `poeOut` number is declared rather than inventing one; the 5 W is the device's own draw, which is what `poeIn` on LAN port 1 means. Only LAN port 1 accepts power in, which is why `poeIn` sits on that port and not on the device. The three ports that do not accept power say `poeIn: 0` explicitly: without it the engine's access-point heuristic would put 12.95 W on all four sockets, which contradicts the page and would make a lab believe any LAN port can feed this box.
